items.name: Jam jar
items.why: Glass jars go in a shared glass container near you, not a bin at home. Dirty is fine, and the lid can stay on.

items.name: Empty wine bottle
items.why: Wine bottles go in a shared glass container. The Omrin Waste App shows the nearest one.

items.name: Broken wine glass
items.why: Drinking glasses don't go in the glass container. A wine glass goes in the Sortibak, with residual waste.

items.name: Used pizza box
items.why: A used, dirty pizza box isn't recyclable paper. It goes in the Sortibak.

items.name: Milk carton
items.why: Drink cartons aren't paper. They go in the Sortibak, and Omrin's machines sort them out afterwards.

items.name: Plastic food packaging
items.why: Plastic goes in the Sortibak. Omrin's machines sort the plastic out afterwards.

items.name: Leftover pasta
items.why: Food leftovers go in the Biobak, or in the shared organic waste container if you live in a flat.

items.name: Cardboard egg carton
items.why: Egg cartons are paper. They go in the paper bin or a paper container.

items.name: Envelope with a window
items.why: Envelopes go in the paper bin, even the ones with a window.

items.name: Clean cardboard box
items.why: Clean cardboard goes in the paper bin or a paper container.

items.name: Torn T-shirt
items.why: Clothes go in the textile container, even worn or torn ones. Put them in a closed plastic bag.

items.name: Old pair of shoes
items.why: Shoes go in the textile container. Tie each pair together.

items.name: Used batteries
items.where: Red KCA box, then the chemokar or the milieustraat
items.why: Batteries are hazardous waste (KCA). Keep them in your red KCA box and hand them in at the chemokar for free.

items.name: Old mattress
items.why: Mattresses go to the milieustraat, for free. Book a time slot and bring your milieupas.

items.name: Used frying oil
items.why: Frying oil doesn't go in any bin. Take it to the milieustraat or your local supermarket.
